description:
## Goal

Every user-visible runtime closure carries one typed, source-derived denotation identity shared by interp, JIT, and AOT. The identity names the source function/lambda, not a transport specialization, code address, allocation, capture-count schema, rendered label, or canonical string. Repeated construction of the same lambda has the same denotation; distinct lambdas do not. Deep copy and GC preserve it verbatim.

This is semantic runtime data. Rendering may display it, but display is only a consumer. fz-5xp.27 will combine it with retained capture values to answer strict closure comparison and map-key identity.

## Current contradiction

The first closure word is called closure_schema_id and ordinary allocation fills it from SchemaRegistry::closure_env(captured_count). Closure layout and tracing already use the header capture count, so this registry entry is vestigial. Equal capture counts collide, schema registration order changes the value, interp and native render different values, and no GC-stable source denotation is available to runtime comparison.

BackendConstructionWrapper.identity is not the answer: it is a specialized TransportPosition. One source lambda can have several wrappers. Promoting its ordinal or canonical display number would make specialization and packaging order semantic.

FunctionId is the exact World identity, but its raw mint number is not a deterministic external order. Retain the typed reverse origin already used to mint a function: named functions are module identity plus source name and arity; generated functions are owner plus structural source position and arity. Package reachable closure denotations in that semantic order and stamp a typed runtime ClosureDenotationId. Do not parse the generated display name to recover owner or position.

## Strategy

- Replace FunctionRef generated-name encoding with a typed named/generated origin while preserving ordinary source names as source identifiers.
- Derive one ClosureDenotationId per reachable source FunctionId at the BackendProgram boundary, independent of activation, CallableId, TransportPosition, wrapper order, schema order, and job order.
- Store that id in the existing first closure word and rename its accessors accordingly. The execution code word remains a separate concern.
- Thread the denotation through every user closure mint, including zero-capture fn refs, construction wrappers, interpreter materialization, JIT/AOT emission, and static closures.
- Preserve it through Cheney copying and cross-heap deep copy.
- Give scheduler/internal continuation scaffolding an explicit typed sentinel and prove it cannot reach user comparison or rendering.
- Delete ClosureEnv schema registration, generated-name parsing, capture-count identity comments, and any duplicate translation tables made obsolete by the cutover.

## Signal

- Two allocations of one lambda at equal captures carry one denotation on every door; two different lambdas with the same arity and capture count carry different denotations.
- One lambda compiled through multiple activation or callable-wrapper specializations still carries one denotation.
- Adding unrelated functions, schemas, or changing job order does not change the packaged denotation order for retained closures.
- Sending a closure and forcing GC preserve the denotation exactly.
- Closure rendering agrees on interp, JIT, and AOT, but no semantic test obtains identity by parsing that rendering.
- Struct schema ids remain correct and byte-identical after ClosureEnv deletion.

## TDD and gates

Begin with red tests at the allocation, packaging, three-door, deep-copy, and GC boundaries. Include a cross-specialization witness, not only equal capture counts. Update semantic-authority, any-value, pipeline, and canonical-form documentation. Full lib, runtime, fixture, CLI, AOT integration, fmt, and warnings-denied clippy gates plus a fresh ticket-scoped cold review precede one commit and close.

comments.text: fz-kdt.209 (filed 2026-09-03) is the sibling of this ticket on the GATE side: test gates assert types by display() output, which is non-injective (fz-go4.34 recorded arrow display collisions; fz-kdt.183 recorded list/non_empty_list collapse). Same root idea as yours -- a rendering is not an identity.

title: [BUG] Give every runtime closure one typed source denotation; delete ClosureEnv schema identity
